about.licence: ODbL 1.0 (share-alike). Contains information from OpenStreetMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors, https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
about.why_separate: Berth positions derived from OpenStreetMap are a Derivative Database under ODbL; they are kept in this file and flagged odbl=true in ships.terminal_berths so the share-alike obligation stays separable. Used only where no USACE / WA Ecology / BC Ports and Terminals row exists.

method.osm_seamark_berth: Overpass centre of one seamark:type=berth way
method.osm_pier_centers: mean of the Overpass centres of the listed man_made=pier ways
method.osm_site_center: Overpass bounding-box centre of the site polygon (low precision)

about.review: lat/lon here are the reviewed values; the import recomputes them from the stored OSM elements and reports drift over 50 m.
about.official_berth: When an OSM berth carries a berth number that the terminal's BC Ports and Terminals berth description also states (e.g. "#1: length 350 m"), official_berth names it; the terminal-calls bake then uses that official length for the radius (lib/ships/terminalCalls.js berthLengthOf). Positions stay OSM; the length is the official record's.
about.added_2026-09-28: Multi-berth fix (Josh 2026-09-28, task 7): Westshore, Neptune, Westridge, Alliance Grain, Cargill, BP Cherry Point, Crofton and Pacific Coast Terminals got the OSM berth/pier elements of berths that lay outside the radius of their single official point (found by stopped AIS positions just outside the radius, 12 sample days). Overpass timestamp_osm_base 2026-09-28T23:02:20Z.
